en: The moon rises, osmanthus blossoms fall
Startling the white egret into flight, and also waking
The street lamps of the mountain village, one by one

points.zh:
人閒桂花落，夜靜春山空。
月出驚山鳥，時鳴春澗中。

en: Dusk slowly rises
In the thin light
Wild geese, departing far

zh: To be or not to be?

Smiling, saying nothing
The spirit of Zen
It is smoke
Must rise to become clouds

zh: 紅色，黄色，藍綠紫  …  白和黑
圓形，方形，三角形  …  點和線
聽，康丁斯基浪漫的幾何音樂
en: Red, yellow, blue-green, violet ... white and black
Circle, square, triangle … dot and line
Listen, to Kandinsky's romantic geometric music

points.zh: 康丁斯基 (Wassily Kandinsky,  1866-1944) 出生於俄國莫斯科，被譽為抽象表現藝術（abstract expressionism）之父，並非只基於他的藝術創作，更因他也是藝術理論家、美學批判以及教育家，這是藝術史上少有的。他的著作如《藝術的精神性》、《點、線、面》等，都是現代藝術理論的經典文獻。他最生動的美學思想，就是「音樂性的藝術喚醒」，或許是從小受古典音樂的薰陶，康丁斯基運用色彩的靈感大多來自音樂：不受視覺限制的音符排列看似自由散漫，實則有著很強的邏輯和秩序，失之毫釐就不能達致「悅耳」的境界。所以康丁斯基的理論和實踐，就是要從色彩、線條和畫布跟内在的心靈產生共鳴，康定斯基在他後期的創作中，融合了自己早期直覺式的畫風和後來的幾何圖形風格，而使他的作品增添了嶄新的理念。他是一位能將色彩與音樂綴合起來的畫家，讓人們能夠「聆聽」繪畫，「描繪」音樂。他説：「顏色是琴鍵，眼睛是琴槌，靈魂是鋼琴的琴絃。藝術家就是演奏的手，撫弄著一個又一個琴鍵，讓靈魂震顫。」（Colour is the keyboard, the eyes are the hammers, the soul is the piano with many strings. The artist is the hand that plays, touching one key or another, to cause vibrations in the soul. ）
points.en: Wassily Kandinsky (1866–1944) was born in Moscow, Russia, and is celebrated as the father of abstract expressionism — not only for his artistic creations, but also because he was a theorist of art, an aesthetic critic, and an educator, a rare combination in art history. His writings, such as 'Concerning the Spiritual in Art' and 'Point and Line to Plane,' are classic texts of modern art theory. His most vivid aesthetic idea was the "musical awakening of art" — perhaps shaped since childhood by classical music, Kandinsky drew much of his inspiration for using color from music: notes arranged with no apparent visual constraint may look freely scattered, yet in fact possess a strong inner logic and order, where the slightest deviation prevents the arrival at a state of "harmony." Thus Kandinsky's theory and practice sought to make color, line, and canvas resonate with the inner spirit. In his later work, he fused his early intuitive painting style with his later geometric style, adding fresh ideas to his art. He was a painter able to fuse color and music, allowing people to "listen" to painting and "paint" music. He said: "Colour is the keyboard, the eyes are the hammers, the soul is the piano with many strings. The artist is the hand that plays, touching one key or another, to cause vibrations in the soul."

en: Beneath the pine I asked the boy
Whether there is a single flower
Quietly fragrant within the clouds and mist?

points.zh:
松下問童子，言師採藥去。
只在此山中，雲深不知處。
--唐。賈島《尋隱者不遇》
points.en:
Beneath the pines I asked the boy;
he said, his master had gone to gather herbs.
He is only somewhere on this mountain,
but the clouds are deep, and I know not where.
-- Tang dynasty. Jia Dao, 'Seeking the Hermit but Not Finding Him'

en: The waves behind push the waves ahead
The leading wave arrives at the bank of the Tamsui River
Startled to see a full setting sun
Venice, may I ask
The seagulls of St. Mark's Square
Do you remember, beyond the sky there is more sky?

points.zh: 聖馬可廣場和嘆息橋是威尼斯的主要地標。聖馬可廣場 (Piazza San Marco) 以及其大教堂總是擠滿來自世界各地的旅客，也是旅客歸去後，對於威尼斯所留下的深刻記憶。馬可是耶穌的門徒，聖經馬可福音書的作者，威尼斯人奉他為護城聖者。相傳兩個威尼斯商人，從埃及亞歷山大把馬聖徒馬可遺骨偷運到威尼斯，并於同年為聖馬可興建教堂。堂內有馬可陵墓，大教堂以聖馬可命名，教堂前面的廣場也得名為聖馬可廣場。19世紀拿破崙贊稱之為「歐洲最美的客廳」。廣埸上最令人驚奇的景象，是密密麻麻的海鷗，安靜時，逐步啄食，驚動時，舉翅齊飛，掩遮廣埸天空，有若掀動的披風，十分壯觀。有謂無鷗不成廣場，是歐洲城市的特色，以聖馬可廣場為最。
points.en: St. Mark's Square and the Bridge of Sighs are the principal landmarks of Venice. St. Mark's Square (Piazza San Marco) and its basilica are always crowded with visitors from all over the world, and it is what travelers remember most vividly of Venice after they return home. Mark was a disciple of Jesus and the author of the Gospel of Mark; the people of Venice revere him as the city's patron saint. According to legend, two Venetian merchants smuggled the relics of St. Mark out of Alexandria, Egypt, to Venice, and a church for St. Mark was built that same year. The basilica houses Mark's tomb, is named after him, and the square in front of it likewise takes its name from him. In the 19th century, Napoleon praised it as "the finest drawing room in Europe." The most astonishing sight in the square is its dense flocks of seagulls — when undisturbed they peck about steadily, but when startled they take flight all at once, filling the sky over the square like a great cloak unfurling, a truly spectacular sight. It is said that no piazza is complete without gulls, a feature distinctive to European cities, and St. Mark's Square is the foremost example.

en: Without bamboo, does one become vulgar?
Dongpo pork, bring another plate
Bamboo shoots stir-fried with shredded pork

points.zh:
「可使食無肉，不可使居無竹，無肉令人瘦，無竹令人俗，人瘦尚可肥，俗士不可醫。」
--宋。蘇軾《於濳僧緑筠軒》
points.en:
"One may eat without meat, but one cannot live without bamboo. Without meat one grows thin; without bamboo one becomes vulgar. A thin person can still be fattened, but a vulgar man cannot be cured."
-- Su Shi (Song dynasty), "At the Bamboo Pavilion of the Monk of Yuqian"

en: Life can be music
Rainbows can be reached
Believe: Tomorrow will be better

points.zh:
《 明天會更好 》
詞：羅大佑 /李壽全 /張大春 /張艾嘉 /詹宏志
曲：羅大佑
日出喚醒清晨
大地光彩重生
讓和風拂出的音響
譜成生命的樂章
唱出你的熱情
伸出你雙手
讓我擁抱著你的夢
讓我擁有你真心的面孔
讓我們的笑容
充滿著青春的驕傲
讓我們期待明天會更好
《 Tomorrow will be better 》
When you wake up in the morning
When you haven't started to think
There is a whole brand new day
Open wide and waiting for you
The world is out there calling
Everything will be alive
under the sunshine's smile
points.en:
"Tomorrow Will Be Better"
Lyrics: Lo Ta-yu / Lee Shou-chuan / Chang Ta-chun / Sylvia Chang / Chan Hung-chih
Music: Lo Ta-yu
Sunrise awakens the morning
the earth is reborn in radiance
let the sound stirred by the gentle breeze
be composed into the music of life
Sing out your passion
hold out your hands
let me embrace your dreams
let me hold your sincere face
let our smiles
be filled with the pride of youth
let us look forward to tomorrow being better
"Tomorrow will be better"
When you wake up in the morning
When you haven't started to think
There is a whole brand new day
Open wide and waiting for you
The world is out there calling
Everything will be alive
under the sunshine's smile
